The science angle is signal integrity: faster chips require shorter, cleaner electrical paths and more advanced board materials.

topic_candidates.title: Does AI Need To Own The RAM In Your PC?
topic_candidates.query: Sam Altman DRAM personal computer data center comments October 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Sam Altman said it was inefficient for limited DRAM to sit in personal computers when it is used only part of the time, triggering backlash from PC owners. The video explains the real trade-off: centralized memory can be shared more efficiently, but local RAM gives people ownership, speed, privacy and the ability to run software offline. It asks whether efficiency is being used to justify moving more computing into rented cloud services.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Tom’s Hardware reported Altman’s October 29 podcast remarks, including his claim that personal-computer DRAM may be used only about 5% of the time. That utilization figure is Altman’s assertion, not an independent measurement. The broader memory squeeze is supported by recent reporting that AI data-center demand is raising pressure on consumer memory supplies. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/openai-ceo-says-its-quite-terrible-for-your-pc-to-have-ram-sam-altman-says-data-centers-offer-better-utilization?utm_source=openai))
topic_candidates.broke_on: November 6, 2026 (approximately; breakout feed marked it 10 hours old)
topic_candidates.science_angle: The difference between local memory and pooled data-center memory: utilization, latency, bandwidth and privacy.
